cover_note: Seven directions, each built on a grid from circles, rectangles and arcs with boolean operations, checked at 16 px, for contrast, and against 96 measured references. Each comes with its system: three circle modes, three lockups and six status poses. Pick one, or name a hybrid.

system_notes.D1: Court Lines. Monoline capitals drawn with the court's own geometry: the trapezoid key A, its crossbar the free-throw line, and the E's middle arm floating free like a painted lane line, lit in clay. Poses use square badges to match its square terminals.
system_notes.D2: Match Day (your direction). Syne ExtraBold lowercase, as in your post: loud, wide and friendly. Each a has its counter filled with a location pin carved into the optical centre of the bowl; both a's match. Accent: pitch green #1F9D63.
system_notes.D3: Live Pin. A map pin whose head is a stadium seen from above, with the live light at its shoulder. The poses replace the light with the status badge, so status always lives in the same place.
system_notes.D4: Convergence Crest. A bracket (four, two, one) carved in a shield: competition and verification in one sign. It scales up to trophy and Verified Arena plaque graphics.
system_notes.D5: Pin in the A. The first A's counter is a map pin standing on the crossbar (find); the last A holds the live light (play). The pin A stands alone as the app icon.
system_notes.D6: Centre Light. The centre circle from the floodlight gantry: two halves split by the halfway line, gathered round the lit spot. It holds best at 16 px of all seven. Never rotate it.
system_notes.D7: Pixel Scoreboard. The GhostRevenue pixel system cloned at your request: square pixels, stepped diagonals, lime / ink / bone / graphite / signal, a pixel pin mascot with six faces that are the app's statuses. Signal red is used only for 'fully booked'.

status_note: The app already speaks in colour: green = Live / Available, amber = Limited, red = Fully Booked, gray = Unavailable. A brand colour that sits on one of those makes every screen ambiguous.

Clear of the status colours: D5 violet, D6 LED cyan. Close to them, and needing a retune if chosen: D1 clay (near the booked red), D4 gold (near amber), D2 pitch green, D3 mint and D7 lime (all near live green).

If a green direction wins (D2, D3, D7), 'Live Now' becomes the brand green with a pulse, 'Available' moves to a neutral outline chip, and every status also carries a shape cue, so nothing relies on colour alone.
In the poses the logo never changes colour; only the badge does. Status belongs to the badge, not the brand.
ranking: D5 Pin in the A (SAD 11/15): the most ownable; the word itself is the arena.
D6 Centre Light (11/15): the best symbol and the best at small sizes; palette and lockup face are the generic parts.
D1 Court Lines (9/15): tasteful but quieter; its clay sits too close to booked red.
D2 Match Day (rebuilt after the review to your brief: Syne, pin counters, green). Its old block-letter scores no longer apply; it now passes every check (nearest reference 0.641).
D3 Live Pin (7/15): reads clearly, but its pin and green sit in the most crowded part of the category.
D4 Convergence Crest (6/15): the shield can read as a trident or menorah, and its navy and gold are close to a major Nigerian bank's.
D7 Pixel Scoreboard (6/15): playful and systemised, but lime on black is the category's most common look; strongest as an illustration and sticker set.
fixed: D5: crossbar under the pin thickened (pin raised, head reduced) so it matches the stems; E–N and R–E tightened.
D1: N–A gap opened from 4 to 8 units.
D6: the halfway-line cut widened from 4 to 6 on the 48 grid, so it survives 16 px.
All poses: the logo no longer turns red or gray; only the badge carries status.
Colour on accent: bone or ink is chosen by contrast, so there is never ink on violet (2.8:1).
Flags recorded (fix if chosen): D4 trident and menorah reading, and bank navy and gold; D3 and D7 green against betting and flag green; D7 mascot face can read as an alien;.
recommendation: Take D5 Pin in the A forward, with D6's Centre Light as a secondary symbol for live states and motion. If you want more noise and attitude for social, D2's Syne voice is a strong campaign face. It shouldn't be the logo as well.
recommendation_detail: Why D5: it's the only direction where the name, the place and the product moment (find, then it's on) are one drawing. Its extracted pin A is a strong, unusual app icon and passes every small-size check.
Why pair it with D6: the split centre circle animates beautifully as the live pulse, so the app has a motion signature without changing the logo.
Violet keeps the brand clear of every status colour and of the crowded green, orange and blue territories in the audit. Bone on violet only.

The reviewer's alternative hybrid, 'Arch & Centre Light' (D5's arch letters with round counters and no pin, plus D6 as the symbol), is cleaner but loses D5's best idea. It's available if you prefer restraint.
This is a recommendation, not a decision: the pick is yours.
